title: Check the design against its target
statement: When review rounds settle into cosmetic findings, check the design against the target it claims to serve, because quiet rounds can hide a real gap.
example: Three rounds of cosmetic findings hid that a writing plan's knowledge-component spine covered only one of the three constructed-response types its target test uses.
detail: Three red-team rounds on a grade 4–5 writing plan converged on naming, counts and cross-references; the fourth deliberately widened the aperture and checked the plan against the test blueprint it claimed to target (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/RED_TEAM_R4.md`). It found that the plan's knowledge-component spine covered only one of the blueprint's three constructed-response types, a gap the package never stated. The gap was then disclosed and mapped rather than rebuilt.
against: The project's review gauntlet ends each layer once it goes dry, at "two consecutive rounds with zero new findings" (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/train-teacher-requirements.md`, lines 164-165), so convergence alone would end a review.

evidence.quote: The convergence to > cosmetics in R1–R3 was masking that nobody had checked the plan against the blueprint it claims to > target — R4 did, and found a gap.
The package targets the STAAR CR blueprint but its KC spine covers only ONE of its three CR types
two consecutive rounds with zero new findings
is a *different* rubric from our internal 8-dimension red-team, so it surfaced gaps our own bar did not weight.
